family: ternary counter on runs of alternating cells
summary: An exact ternary counter, least significant digit at the left end, whose digits are pairs of long runs of alternating cells read mod 4; the increment is proved in Lean for every carry depth, and so is the shuttle that moves a run to the right end when a shrinking run runs out. Open: the whole transfer (it nests) and an invariant; tapes with the same residues and short runs do halt.
title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is an exact ternary counter: its digits are pairs of runs of alternating cells, valued by their lengths mod 4, and each trip of the head adds one. That increment is proved in Lean (kernel) for every carry depth, and it covers 99.86% of the trips in the first 3·1012 steps. The counter keeps shrinking one run of each digit; when such a run runs out, a transfer moves a long run to the right end of the tape, two cells per shuttle of the head. The shuttle itself is now proved in Lean for every list of runs in between and any number of shuttles, and so are the events at a run boundary, including the one pattern that halts.

What is missing is the transfer as a whole (the shuttles before the tail is “saturated”, transfers nested inside transfers, the pairing of the digits afterwards) and an invariant. The invariant cannot be about residues alone: tapes with exactly the residues of a real configuration but several short runs do halt (for example 6 6 4 6 5 5 5 5 6 7 at step 5,943). In the real run every transfer of the first 1014 steps has long runs to spare, but that is an observation, not a proof.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 76,685 cells have been visited and 38,338 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.389).

claims.title: Sweep moves
claims.text: L A>(0101)^n R → L (1010)^n A> R (4n steps: going right A flips the phase of a block), L (01)^n B>0 R → L B>0 (01)^n R and L (10)^n C>1 R → L C>1 (10)^n R (2n steps: going left blocks are crossed unchanged), for every n, L, R.

claims.title: The pieces of a trip
claims.text: Eight rules for all run lengths and every surrounding tape: digit 0 going from 0 to 1 and from 1 to 2 (whole trips), the carry leaving digit 0, the carry passing a digit at 2 (a bounce), the carry stopping at a digit at 1 or at 0, and going home over a passed digit and over digit 0, with exact step counts.

claims.title: The increment, for every carry depth
claims.text: By induction over the list of digits a carry passes: from the start of a trip with digit 0 at 2, any number of digits at 2, then a digit at 1 (or at 0), the machine reaches the start of the next trip with the exact tape and step count stated. With inc0 and inc1 this is every kind of trip while the runs involved are long enough (r0 ≥ 7, r1 ≥ 5, a passed digit x ≥ 9, y ≥ 5, the stopping digit x ≥ 4, y ≥ 6 or x ≥ 6, y ≥ 7).

claims.title: The run-length table of a trip
claims.text: Read off the Lean statements: digit 0 changes (r0, r1) by (+2, +3) and takes one cell from x1, by (+5, −1), or by (+1, +2) when it carries; a passed digit changes by (−2, +2), a digit going from 1 to 2 by (+2, −1), from 0 to 1 by (−1, +3) and takes one cell from the next digit. Checked by expanding the statements for 2,000 random parameter choices.

claims.title: An exact fast simulator
claims.text: py/rsim.py runs the machine on a run-length tape with the three proved sweep moves; it agrees with a plain cell simulator on the step of every one of the 17,669 trip starts in the first 4·109 steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>14</sup> steps
claims.text: py/rsim.py runs 1014 steps without a halt (3,153,668 trips).

claims.title: 99.86% of trips are the proved kinds
claims.text: Of the 726,270 trips in the first 3·10<sup>12</sup> steps, 725,254 have one of the four proved shapes with the runs long enough. Of the other 1,016, the carry reaches the right end in 98, a run is too short in 269, and a digit has residues outside the table in 648 (and one is the first trip). They come, as far as we have looked, with transfers (a run x<sub>k</sub> has run out and the run y<sub>k−1</sub> is shuttled, two cells at a time, to the right end of the tape, after which the digits past it are paired anew) or with the right end, where new digits are made from short runs.

claims.title: How close it comes to halting
claims.text: The machine halts exactly when D reads a 1 whose left neighbour is a 1. Of the 6,032,756 times D read a 1 in the first 3·10<sup>12</sup> steps, the alternating stretch ending at D's cell had length 2 158 times and length 3 17 times (a halt needs length 1); those we looked at were near the right end or in transfers.

claims.title: The events at a run boundary
claims.text: For every surrounding tape: going right, A passes a boundary (run length 0 or 3 mod 4, counted from A on a 0) or turns (1 or 2 mod 4); going left, the head crosses a 00 boundary and moves it two cells, bounces at a 11 boundary, or, on a run 1 0 of exactly two cells between 11 and 00, halts four steps later. Both passes flip every cell they cross.

claims.title: The shuttle of a transfer, for every tail and any number of shuttles
claims.text: L (10)^m 0 A> 1(0101)^(a1+1) … 1(0101)^(an+1) 1(0101)^z 0^inf becomes the same tape with (10)^m removed and the last run 1(0101)^(z+m), in exactly m(2S + 8z + 8) + 4m(m − 1) steps (S = total length of the n runs in between): 2m cells leave the moved run, 4m arrive at the right end, nothing in between changes. By induction over the list of runs and over m.

claims.title: Tapes with the same residues and short runs halt
claims.text: Real trip starts with every long run replaced by the smallest length of the same residue mod 4 halt in 20 of 2,692 cases (threshold 4): 6 6 4 6 5 5 5 5 6 7 halts at step 5,943 and 6 6 2 7 9 6 6 7 7 7 5 at step 1,005, both confirmed on a plain cell-by-cell simulator. With every long run cut to its shortest length of 8 or more cells none halted (0 of 9,155 shortened tapes at threshold 8, and none at 10, 12, 16; 3 of 7,119 at threshold 6). One run changed by ±1 or ±2 halts in about 4% of the cases; long runs replaced by random lengths of the same residue never did (0 of 3,829). So an invariant must fix the residues and bound lengths from below.

claims.title: Tools checked against the real run and by mutation
claims.text: Building a trip start from a list of runs and running to the next one reproduces 14,387 consecutive trip starts of the real run (list and step count). The shuttle statement agrees with a plain simulator in 200 of 200 random cases, and five mutated statements fail in 40 of 40 cases each.

claims.title: Transfers nest, and the right end is the same counter one level deeper
claims.text: A shuttle of a transfer can become a whole inner transfer (trip 2,225,395: an inner transfer of 10,807 shuttles inside an outer one of about 55). The runs behind a freshly deposited run go through exactly the states the whole tape went through from the start (125, 69 and 35 states compared, all equal), three times slower per level; after a transfer the digit pairs take residues outside the table for a few carries (14 of the 16 classes occur).

claims.title: Every transfer of the first 10<sup>14</sup> steps ends saturated
claims.text: In 3,153,668 trips there are 168 transfers or nested levels with at least 3 shuttles; each ends with at least 6 saturated shuttles (the proved kind), after at most 20 unsaturated ones (60 in one level containing two inner transfers). D read a 1 63,281,275 times; the alternating stretch ending there was 2 cells long 218 times and 3 cells 21 times, never 1 (a halt). A candidate regular invariant (windows of 3 runs, lengths below 8 exact, else mod 4) did not stabilise: 263 windows, new ones still at 3.9·10<sup>13</sup> steps.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof needs the transfer as a rule (saturation, nesting, merges, entry and exit), the regular trips for the residue classes that follow a transfer, and an invariant that bounds each moved run from below by the size of the tail behind it; a halt would need several long runs to be short at the same time.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LD_1LD0RF_1RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine counts in base 3, least significant digit at the left end. Its tape is a row of long runs of alternating cells; each pair of neighbouring runs is a digit, valued by the run lengths mod 4, and every trip of the head from the left end and back adds one. The increment is proved, and so is the shuttle that carries a run to the far end when a digit's run is used up; the full transfer and an invariant are not.

facts.text: The increment of the counter, for any carry, proved in Lean.
The shuttle of a transfer: 2m cells leave, 4m arrive, proved in Lean.
Share of the trips in 3·10<sup>12</sup> steps that are the proved kinds.
A tape with the residues of a real one but short runs halts.
No halt in the exact run-length simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.389).
After 109 steps the tape spans 76,685 cells (39,628 left of the start, 15,538 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Runs of alternating cells
html: Cut the tape into maximal runs of alternating cells, 0101… or 1010…. Two neighbouring runs meet at a doubled cell, 00 or 11, so the list of run lengths says everything (the first run starts with 0). At the start of a trip (A at the left end) the runs are, at step 10,000,025,550:
Name them r0 r1 | x1 y1 | x2 y2 | …: digit 0 is (r0, r1), digit k is (xk, yk).

sections.heading: A counter in base 3
html: A digit's value is read from its two run lengths mod 4:

valuedigit 0 (r0, r1) mod 4digit k (x, y) mod 4
0(0, 3)(2, 3)
1(2, 2)(0, 2)
2(3, 1)(1, 1)
(After digit k changes, xk can be one cell longer than this reading, until digit k−1 next goes from 0 to 1 and takes that cell.) Each trip adds one, and the runs change by a few cells:

digitchangeruns
00 → 1r0 + 2, r1 + 3, x1 − 1
01 → 2r0 + 5, r1 − 1
02 → 0, carryr0 + 1, r1 + 2
k2 → 0, carryx − 2, y + 2
k1 → 2x + 2, y − 1
k0 → 1x − 1, y + 3, next x − 1

Going right, A flips every cell it passes. A carry is a bounce: B meets the 00 at the start of xk, runs back over yk−1, turns, and goes on through digit k. Where the carry stops the head turns and goes home, B and C carrying the pattern one cell along; the left end grows by 4 cells per trip.
All of this is proved in Lean, for all run lengths and for every carry depth at once (an induction over the digits the carry passes): trip_stop1, trip_stop0, inc0, inc1 in lean/Counter.lean.

sections.heading: Runs that run out
html: Over one cycle of digit k (3k+1 trips) xk loses 4 cells and yk gains 4, so every xk eventually runs out. Then the next carry does not bounce through: the head shuttles between the end of yk−1 and the right end of the tape, moving yk−1 two cells at a time to the far right (a transfer; these are the long pauses of the run and the reason the right side grows). Afterwards the digits past it are paired anew and counting goes on. For example at step 39,282 the runs 187 97 2 31 25 7 7 have become 186 43 27 5 13 177.

In the first 3·1012 steps 99.86% of the 726,270 trips are the proved kinds; the rest come with transfers. The right end is not a separate mechanism: the runs behind a freshly deposited run replay the whole tape's own history, three times slower per level.

sections.heading: A transfer, shuttle by shuttle
html: During a transfer the head enters the runs behind the moved run one cell out of phase. A run that starts with a 1 and has length 1 mod 4 lets it through (it is saturated); any other run turns it back and is changed, so the first shuttles each repair one run:

moved runruns behind it (after the head's cell)
9733 24 7 7first shuttle
9536 23 7 72 cells taken per shuttle
9336 26 6 7
9136 29 5 7
8936 29 5 7 7a new run at the right end
8736 29 5 10 6
8536 29 5 13 5
8336 29 5 13 9saturated: only the last run changes now, +4 per shuttle
136 29 5 13 173the moved run is used up

The saturated shuttle is proved in Lean for every list of runs in between and every number m of shuttles: L (10)^m 0 A> 1(0101)^(a+1) … 1(0101)^z becomes L 0 A> 1(0101)^(a+1) … 1(0101)^(z+m) in m(2S + 8z + 8) + 4m(m − 1) steps (shuttles, scst_eq in lean/Transfer.lean, by induction over the list and over m). The events at a single run boundary are proved too (loc_pass0 … loc_halt).

Not proved: the shuttles before saturation for an arbitrary tail, and two complications seen in the real run. Transfers nest: a shuttle can turn at an inner digit whose own run is used up and become a complete inner transfer (at trip 2,225,395 an inner transfer of 10,807 shuttles runs inside an outer one of about 55). And a carry that meets a run of a single cell merges three runs into one.

sections.eyebrow: Why it is not a proof yet
sections.heading: Nearby tapes halt
html: The sibling proofs in this group keep the long counts free and track only remainders. The first test for that is whether nearby tapes halt. Here they do:

change to a real configurationtapes that halt
one run ±290 of 2,510
one run ±174 of 1,698
every long run replaced by a random length of the same residue mod 40 of 3,829
every run of 4 or more cells replaced by the shortest length of its residue20 of 2,692

So the residues are essential, and the lengths are almost free but not quite: 6 6 4 6 5 5 5 5 6 7 has the residues of the real 3106 1606 56 506 429 93 5 29 26 7 and halts at step 5,943. Several runs are used up at nearly the same time, a transfer moves a run of only 13 cells and ends before the tail is saturated, and the short run it leaves is later worn down to 2 cells, the halting pattern. With every long run cut to its shortest length of 8 or more cells none halted (0 of 9,155 shortened tapes at threshold 8, and none at 10, 12, 16; 3 of 7,119 at threshold 6).

An invariant therefore has to bound lengths from below, and not by a constant: the moved run must outlast the saturation of the tail behind it, which can contain whole inner transfers. In the real run every transfer of the first 1014 steps ends with at least 6 saturated shuttles and usually thousands; that is why it has not halted, but it is not yet a proof.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The only halting transition is F on a 1. F comes from E (on a cell B has just made 0, so F reads that 0) or from D, and D only from C on a 0. So the machine halts exactly when D reads a 1 whose left neighbour is also a 1: the head, going left, steps onto a run 1 0 of exactly two cells between a 11 and a 00 (loc_halt). In the proved trips that never happens. In the first 1014 steps D read a 1 about 63 million times; the alternating stretch ending at D's cell was 2 cells long 218 times and 3 cells long 21 times (a halt needs 1).
So a halt, if any, would come from a transfer. The exact simulator finds none in 1014 steps.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
